problem: Astro MDX parser crashes during build when rendering standard mathematical formulas or text containing curly braces { }.
solution: The MDX compiler interprets anything inside `{}` as a JavaScript expression. Never use raw curly braces in MDX files. Solution: Always use square brackets `[]` or escape the curly braces using backslashes `\{ \}`.
impact: Prevents catastrophic build failures across the entire content pipeline.

problem: White-background JPEG illustrations look terrible and break the aesthetic when a user switches the website to Dark Mode.
solution: Apply a specific CSS filter chain to the image tag: `mix-blend-multiply dark:invert dark:mix-blend-screen`. This dynamically drops the white background in light mode and intelligently inverts the colors while retaining transparency in dark mode.
impact: Maintains premium visual aesthetic across 100% of articles without requiring duplicate image assets.

problem: Textbook algebraic formulas create high cognitive load, causing readers to lose attention and bounce from the page.
solution: Never use static math formulas (`A - B = C`). Instead, build interactive Astro Workbench components (like `Penalty270AWorkbench` or `NoticePenaltyWorkbench`). Use visual toggles, range sliders, and dynamic color changes (e.g., turning the UI red when a penalty triggers).
impact: Dramatically increases reader retention and intuitively communicates complex tax mechanics.

problem: Long article titles (80+ characters) cause breadcrumb components to wrap onto multiple lines, breaking the top-level layout grid.
solution: Apply strict `max-width` and `truncate` CSS classes to the final breadcrumb item to enforce a single line with an ellipsis (`...`). Ensure zero SEO loss by retaining the full, untruncated string in the underlying `JSON-LD` Schema script.
impact: Guarantees a pixel-perfect, MacOS-style breadcrumb navigation bar regardless of title length.

problem: Running the Astro dev server locks up the terminal window, preventing concurrent file modifications and command executions.
solution: Always start the development server in background mode using `astro dev --background`. Manage the background process using `astro dev stop`, `astro dev status`, and `astro dev logs`.
impact: Unlocks the terminal for concurrent workflow and faster iterative development.
